name: Sarah Chaney
current_role: Cargill heir (no known operating role); listed as Sarah MacMillan on LA Business Journal's 2017 Wealthiest Angelenos
profile: Cargill-MacMillan family heir, one of four daughters of the late W. Duncan MacMillan; media reports estimated each daughter inherited roughly a 3% stake in Cargill, the largest privately held US company. Appears to be the same person as 'Sarah MacMillan' (LABJ #49, 2017, $1.35B). Keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She is a great-great-granddaughter of W.W. Cargill, who started Cargill as a single grain storage business in Conover, Iowa, in 1865.
notes: Very private; no public role, accounts or published contacts found. Identity link Chaney = MacMillan rests on LABJ and a LittleSis listing rather than a primary source; LABJ's stated age (28 in 2017) looks inconsistent. Not a good podcast target.

name: Shi Yonghong
current_role: Chairman, Yihai International (HK:1579); co-founder and director of Haidilao International
profile: Co-founded Sichuan hot pot chain Haidilao in Jianyang in 1994 with Zhang Yong and their wives, each pair putting in a small share of an 8,000-yuan start. Haidilao listed in Hong Kong in 2018; Shi and wife Li Haiyan also hold stakes in spun-off condiment maker Yihai International, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Haidilao is known for extreme service touches such as free manicures for waiting customers, and has expanded to the US, Japan, South Korea and Singapore.
deep_cut_fact: Shi met his future co-founder Zhang Yong as a schoolmate at a vocational school in Jianyang, Sichuan, where Zhang was studying electric welding; that friendship became the four-person founding team of Haidilao's first four-table shop in March 1994.
notes: Low public profile compared with Zhang Yong; Yihai chairman role per etnet company page (https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=1579). Best route is Haidilao/Yihai IR or media office. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Gu Jiangsheng
current_role: Director (former chairman) of Kuka Home (顾家家居, SSE:603816)
profile: Built Hangzhou upholstered-furniture maker Kuka Home out of his father Gu Yuhua's furniture business, rebranding it as 'Kuka' around 2000 and listing it in Shanghai in 2016. In 2023-24 the Gu family sold ~29% to Midea heir He Jianfeng's Infore group (~8.9bn yuan), and Gu stepped down as chairman in Sept 2024 while staying on the board.
interesting_fact: Control of Kuka Home passed in January 2024 from the Gu family to He Jianfeng, son of Midea founder He Xiangjian, with ex-Midea executive Kuang Guangxiong taking over as chairman.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family furniture business from his father around 2000 and renaming it 'Kuka Craft Sofa', Gu was a physical education teacher (Yicai describes him as a former university PE teacher; other profiles say he studied in Hangzhou University's PE department).
notes: No longer controls the company; no IR email found in quick search (check latest 603816 annual report on sse.com.cn). Avoid the 2020 CSRC probe topic.

name: Zhou Xiaoping
current_role: Chairwoman and CEO, Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems (SSE:601799)
profile: Founded Xingyu in 1993 with her late father Zhou Bajin, growing it into China's leading private auto-lamp maker supplying VW, Mercedes-Benz, BMW and GM; it listed in Shanghai in 2011. 2025 revenue was about 15.3bn yuan; the company filed for a Hong Kong 'A+H' listing in 2026 and set up a robotics JV with Jaka in 2025.
interesting_fact: Xingyu was the first private Chinese auto-lighting company to list on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (2011).
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a doctor (Norman Bethune University of Medical Sciences, 1990) and was vice principal of Wujin Health School in Changzhou before leaving at 32 to start an auto-lamp factory on about 112,000 yuan of borrowed money.
notes: IR contact (board secretary Gao Peng) is listed in Xingyu's SSE filings; no email captured here. Chinese-language outreach via company IR advisable.

name: Zhang Yue'e
current_role: Co-founder, Lepu Medical (乐普医疗, SZSE:300003); founder of PW Medtech (普华和顺); current title not confirmed
profile: Materials scientist who, with husband Pu Zhongjie, returned from the US in 1999 to co-found Lepu Medical, one of China's earliest makers of cardiovascular interventional devices (ChiNext listing 2009). She separately founded high-end device maker PW Medtech, listed in Hong Kong in 2013. The couple appeared on Hurun's 2022 global list with about 15bn yuan.
interesting_fact: The 'Lepu family' of companies keeps spinning off: structural-heart unit Xintai Medical was carved out of Lepu Medical for a Hong Kong listing.
deep_cut_fact: She and her husband share the same academic path: both graduated from Xi'an Jiaotong University and both later did graduate study at Florida International University in Miami before coming home to start Lepu.
notes: Wealth listed jointly with husband Pu Zhongjie (Lepu chairman). Very low personal profile; route via Lepu Medical board office/IR (contacts in SZSE filings). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Patrick Hanrahan
current_role: Canon USA Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering, Stanford University; Tableau co-founder
profile: Computer-graphics pioneer who co-founded data-visualization company Tableau in 2003 out of his Stanford research; Salesforce bought it in 2019 for $15.7bn. Earlier a founding Pixar employee and chief architect of the RenderMan Interface; he shared the 2019 ACM Turing Award with Ed Catmull and still teaches at Stanford.
interesting_fact: Won three Academy Awards for technical work (RenderMan in 1993, subsurface light scattering in 2004, physically based rendering in 2014) and is credited on Tin Toy and Toy Story.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Green Bay, Wisconsin, earned a B.S. in nuclear engineering at UW-Madison (1977) and a PhD in biophysics (1985); as a grad student he taught a new graphics course in 1981 whose early students included future visualization artist Donna Cox.
notes: Email is his Stanford faculty address published on his own homepage. Academic, approachable profile; strong fit for a data/data-center angle (GPUs, rendering, visualization). Turing Award news: https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2020/03/pat-hanrahan-wins-turing-award

name: Guy Laliberté
current_role: Founder, Lune Rouge (Montreal investment/creative firm); founder, One Drop Foundation
profile: Former street performer who co-founded Cirque du Soleil in 1984 and built it into a global entertainment giant; sold 90% to TPG/Fosun in 2015 and his last 10% to CDPQ in 2020. Now invests in arts, tech and entertainment through Lune Rouge, runs the One Drop water foundation, and hosts the Big Deal for One Drop charity poker event in Las Vegas.
interesting_fact: In 2009 he became the first Canadian private space traveller (Soyuz TMA-16), using the trip for a 'water awareness' webcast spanning 14 cities on five continents and the ISS.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cirque took off he hitchhiked around Europe at 18 playing accordion, learned fire-eating and stilt-walking, and once took a full-time job at a hydroelectric dam in Quebec, returning to street performing only when the dam workers went on strike.
notes: Hydro-dam job is a natural hook for an energy podcast. Lune Rouge is his personal investment vehicle and the best route. Avoid the 2019 Tahiti cannabis episode and space-trip tax case.

name: Liang Changlin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Dingdong Maicai (Dingdong Fresh); stepped down as CEO in 2026 after Meituan agreed to acquire the company
profile: Army veteran (12 years' service) turned serial entrepreneur in Shanghai's Zhangjiang: built video software, then mother-and-baby community Yaya.com (sold to TAL in 2016), then founded fresh-grocery e-commerce platform Dingdong Maicai in 2017, listing it on the NYSE in 2021. In 2026 Meituan agreed to buy Dingdong for about US$717m; Liang handed the CEO role to CFO Wang Song and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Named on China's 2020 national honour roll of veteran entrepreneurs ('全国退役军人创业光荣榜') for job creation.
deep_cut_fact: His first pot of gold came from a piece of software: shortly after leaving the army in 2002 he wrote 'Easy Video Joiner & Splitter', billed as the first video cut-and-join tool, and sold about 50,000 copies worldwide for roughly US$800,000.
notes: Meituan deal and CEO change per Jiemian (https://www.jiemian.com/article/14091669.html); IR mailbox may change once Dingdong is absorbed into Meituan. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Tom Steyer
current_role: Co-founder, Galvanize Climate Solutions (took leave in 2025 to run for California governor; conceded after June 2026 primary)
profile: Founded hedge fund Farallon Capital in 1986 and grew it to about $20bn before leaving in 2012 to focus on climate and politics. Co-founded climate investor Galvanize with Katie Hall in 2021, ran for president in 2020 and for California governor in 2026, finishing third in the June 2026 top-two primary. Author of 'Cheaper, Faster, Better: How We'll Win the Climate War' (2024).
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and his wife Kat Taylor gave $41 million to create the TomKat Center for Sustainable Energy at Stanford; they also founded Beneficial State Bank, whose stock is held by a foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He captained the Yale soccer team, and named Farallon after the Farallon Islands off the Bay Area coast; Yale's endowment, after first turning him down, became an early client in 1987 with Farallon managing its money at no fee.
notes: Very media-accessible and a natural energy/climate-investing guest. Galvanize lists the press address for media inquiries. Primary result: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/billionare-tom-steyer-ends-california-governor-campaign-falling-short-jungle-primary.print ; post-campaign role at Galvanize not confirmed.

name: Antti Aarnio-Wihuri
profile: Born in Turku in 1940, he heads the Wihuri Group, a 120-year-old Finnish family conglomerate (packaging, technical trade incl. Caterpillar dealerships, Metro wholesale, aviation, jet charter and air ambulance) with about 5,000 staff. He is also the largest shareholder of Canadian packaging maker Winpak.
interesting_fact: A former racing driver and team principal: his AAW Racing Team won the European Interserie championship three times in the early 1970s with driver Leo Kinnunen.
deep_cut_fact: He raced himself in the 1960s, taking class wins at Finnish circuits Artukainen, Keimola and Rovaniemi in 1966 and entering the 1000 km Nürburgring four years running (1967-70); he later backed young drivers including Valtteri Bottas.
notes: Aged 86, private. Board role per Finnish registry (https://www.asiakastieto.fi/yritykset/fi/wihuri-oy/25578562/paattajat). Group general mailbox is the only published route.

name: Theodore Lerner
profile: Deceased. Washington-area real estate developer (Lerner Enterprises, founded 1952) and founding principal owner of the Washington Nationals; died 12 February 2023 at age 97.

name: Suh Kyung-bae
profile: Second-generation head of Amorepacific, South Korea's largest cosmetics maker (Sulwhasoo, Laneige, Innisfree), founded by his father Suh Sung-whan in 1945. Took over in 1997 and rode the K-beauty/Hallyu wave into global markets; Forbes Asia named him Businessman of the Year in 2015. Also funds basic life-science research through his own foundation.
interesting_fact: Amorepacific traces its roots to his grandmother, who sold camellia oil as a hair treatment across the Korean peninsula; in the 1960s the company built a door-to-door saleswomen network, some of them Korean War widows.
deep_cut_fact: His Suh Kyungbae Science Foundation (founded 2016) backs young Korean life scientists with long-term grants (31 SUHF Fellows by 2025); in his chairman's message he cites the phrase 'Beyond the sky there is another sky' (天外有天), which also names the foundation newsletter 'Beyond the Sky'.
notes: Foundation mailbox (he chairs it) is the most personal published route; corporate PR via Amorepacific. Bio details: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suh_Kyung-bae. Foundation history: https://www.suhf.org/introduce/history.do
